pattern.top_pattern: Unattributed and Not Mapped outpatient claims are obscuring specialty drug and ancillary spend
pattern.what_is_impacting: UNATTRIBUTED / CA / GA / TX outpatient drugs, lab, supplies, and OP ER
pattern.pattern_details: Large outpatient spend is landing in UNATTRIBUTED and Not Mapped categories, dominated by hemophilia-related drug claims and smaller clusters in lab, supplies, and maternity-related OP ER claims. That limits visibility into who should own the spend and whether the claims are in the right clinical bucket. This should be resolved before any broad utilization interpretation is used for action.
pattern.why_it_matters: Misclassified outpatient claims can hide the real source of cost pressure and misroute follow-up work across clinical, UM, and data teams.
pattern.recommended_next_step: Reconcile attribution and clinical classification for Not Mapped outpatient claims, starting with D66 and D67 drug claims, then confirm the correct provider, setting, and category for the smaller lab, supplies, and OP ER items.
pattern.validation_reason: The leading claims are either UNATTRIBUTED or Not Mapped, so ownership and classification need to be fixed before trend action is assigned.
evidence_summary: UNATTRIBUTED D66 outpatient drug spend added about $1.6M.
UNATTRIBUTED D67 outpatient drug spend added about $0.7M across 8 more claims.
GA lab and pathology claims at THREE RIVERS DIAGNOSTICS added about $10K across 163 claims and remained Not Mapped.
Smaller Not Mapped items also appeared in CA supplies and TX OP ER maternity claims.
